name: Portaly
subcategory: creator link pages with payments and booking blocks
tagline: A hosted link-in-bio page builder for creators, with blocks for links, products, tickets and bookings.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: A link-in-bio page is a list of links with a photo on top, and that has been a one-file build since the invention of CSS. An agent can produce a mobile-first page with an editable config, click tracking and a theme in a single sitting, and hosting it costs nothing. The parts that are genuinely hard are the commerce bits: selling tickets, taking card payments, syncing a booking calendar, all of which mean Stripe plus real support burden when a payment fails. If your bio link is just links, build it and never think about it again. If it is your storefront, the hosted version is doing work you would rather not own.
coreLoopDIY: Renders a mobile-first public profile page from a config file with avatar, bio, themed link buttons and social icons, and logs clicks to a local database you can view on a private stats page.
requirements: A domain or subdomain to point at it
Somewhere to host a small Next.js app, a free tier is fine
Your own Stripe account if you want to sell anything
whatYouLose: Payments, digital products and ticketing without wiring up Stripe and handling refunds yourself
Booking and calendar blocks that actually sync to a real calendar
A visual editor, so every change is a code or config edit
Polished mobile-optimised templates and preview cards that already look right in every app's in-app browser
Analytics dashboards, UTM handling and pixel integrations that marketers expect
moatNotes: The defensible part is not the page, it is the payment and ticketing plumbing bolted onto it, plus localised support for a specific creator market.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the page is the cheap part. Creators pay for the checkout that works on a phone in an Instagram in-app browser, the ticket QR codes that scan at the door, the payout that lands, and someone to email when it does not. Also because editing a page from your phone between posts beats opening a code editor, and a lot of the target users have never opened one.
notes: Link-in-bio remains the most-cloned category in software, for the obvious reason: it is a list.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted link-in-bio page. Stack: Next.js with the App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, SQLite via better-sqlite3. No auth provider, no analytics SDK, no telemetry.

In scope:
1. A single public route at / that renders my profile page: avatar image, display name, short bio, a vertical stack of large tappable link buttons, and a row of social icons at the bottom.
2. All content comes from one file, content.ts, exporting a typed config: profile (name, bio, avatarUrl, theme), links (array of id, label, optional sublabel, url, optional emoji or icon name, optional highlighted flag), socials (array of platform, url).
3. Three themes selectable by a string in the config: light, dark, and a gradient theme. Implement them with Tailwind classes and CSS variables, no theme library.
4. Mobile-first layout, max width around 480px, centred, large touch targets, works fine on desktop too.
5. Click tracking: every link is an internal route /go/[id] that records a row (link id, timestamp, referrer, coarse user agent) into SQLite, then 302s to the target URL. Redirect must not block on the write failing.
6. A stats page at /stats, protected by HTTP Basic Auth using ADMIN_USER and ADMIN_PASS from .env. Show total clicks per link, clicks in the last 7 days, and a simple bar list. No charting library, use divs.
7. Proper metadata: title, description, Open Graph and Twitter card tags pulled from the config, plus a favicon and a static OG image file.
8. A /health route returning ok.

Out of scope, do not build: payments, product sales, ticketing, booking calendars, a visual drag and drop editor, multi-user accounts, email capture, or a CMS.

Deliverables: working app, seed content.ts with three placeholder links, .env.example listing ADMIN_USER and ADMIN_PASS and DATABASE_PATH, a migration that creates the clicks table on boot if missing, and a README with local dev, deploy notes for a single small VPS or a container, and instructions for pointing a custom domain at it. Run the app and confirm the page renders and a click is recorded before you finish.
